validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, real physical pipeline, not phantom. At least 8 mutually independent sources describe this specific named project ('Noorus/Nooros-Abu Madi-El Gamil'): (1) Egyptian Presidency official project page (title match, blocked from direct fetch by bot-wall but confirmed via search); (2) Al-Ahram Gate news (gate.ahram.org.eg) headline 'El-Molla follows up executive status of the Nooros-Abu Madi-El Gamil pipeline project'; (3) sfegypt.com Ministry of Petroleum readout (already the sheet's own Start/Diameter/SegmentCost ref) with direct quote confirming the project; (4) Daily News Egypt (dailynewsegypt.com, 2019-11-20); (5) Egypt Oil & Gas (egyptoil-gas.com); (6) petro-news.com Ministry-achievements compilation (item #33 in a numbered projects list); (7) Eni's own corporate site (eni.com) describing Nooros field production feeding this same corridor; (8) SARI Engineering's project list (client PETROBEL, 'EL GAMIL' project) and DMS Universe/DMS Projects industry project database ('Petrobel - Nooros - Abu Madi - El Gamil Gas Pipeline'). None of these trace back to GEM or to a single wire story - independent origins (government, two different trade press outlets, an EPC-adjacent engineering firm, a commercial project-intelligence database, and the field operator's own site).
CLASSIFICATION: correct as gas transmission trunk. It is an onshore, two-segment trunk (Nooros wellhead/tie-in -> Abu Madi gas treatment plant -> El Gamil gas treatment plant -> Egyptian national gas grid), explicitly described as feeding the national grid ('ضخه في الشبكة القومية للغازات الطبيعية' - petro-news.com); not a gathering/plant-internal line.
DUPLICATE: checked against the full 30-row Egypt-gas-operating roster and the full GulfPub Egypt gas roster (95 features). No overlap found. The nearby GEM rows P5132/P6036 (Zohr-Al Gamil, Shorouk concession) and P6037 (Al Gamil-Damietta) are different fields/concessions and different corridors. GulfPub's Egypt list has several other 'Abu Madi' lines (Nidoco-Abu Madi 6km, Baltim East-Abu Madi 18km, Delta East-Abu Madi 17km, Abu Madi-Tanta 50-52km, Abu Madi-El Mansura 24km) but none of these match this row's specs (130km, 24/32in, Nooros field origin, El Gamil terminus) - they are shorter, different-diameter field tie-ins into the Abu Madi hub, not this trunk. One AI-search-synthesis answer momentarily conflated this line with a separate 'Nidoco-Abu Madi' project (Nidoco is a distinct, later-discovered field in the same 'Great Nooros Area'); primary sources (sfegypt.com, petro-news.com) consistently and unambiguously name Nooros, not Nidoco, as this pipeline's field origin, so this is not treated as a duplicate/mislabel - just a caution noted for the record.
SPEC checks: Length 130km - CONFIRMED verbatim by sfegypt.com (sheet's own ref): 'مشروع مد خط بري بطول 130 كم' (onshore line, 130 km). One secondary aggregator (industry search synthesis, provenance unclear, likely from a contractor project sheet) cites '126 km' for the same corridor - a minor variance (~3%), plausibly a different measurement point (wellhead vs. plant tie-in) or rounding; not enough to override the primary Ministry-sourced 130km figure, but noted as a small residual discrepancy. Diameter 24,32in - CONFIRMED verbatim ('وقطر 24 و 32 بوصة') by the same source. Capacity 700 Mcf/d - CONFIRMED independently and repeatedly (Daily News Egypt, Egypt Oil & Gas, alborsaanews.com, petro-news.com, DMS Universe/DMS Projects) - all cite 700 million cubic feet/day. SegmentCost $300,000,000 - CONFIRMED independently (sfegypt.com 'باستثمارات بلغت حوالى 300مليون دولار'; Daily News Egypt '$300m'; Egypt Oil & Gas '$300 million'; petro-news.com 'بتكلفة 300 مليون دولار'). Note: the worklist's automated existing_ref_check flagged Status [ref] (petro-news.com) and SegmentCost [ref] (sfegypt.com) as FAIL because the literal strings 'operating' / '300,000,000' don't appear - these are the documented false-negative pattern (status is inferable from context, not a literal token; cost is spelled out in words '300 مليون دولار' rather than digits). Both pages, read directly, DO support the cited values - status is confirmed by 'تم تشغيل الخط في مايو 2019' (line put into operation May 2019) on sfegypt.com and by the project's inclusion in petro-news.com's completed-achievements list; cost is confirmed by the prose figure above. Both existing refs should be KEPT, not treated as broken. StartYear1 2019 - CONFIRMED (May 2019, '7 months ahead of the 2019 target date' per sfegypt.com; consistent with the November 2019 Daily News Egypt/Egypt Oil & Gas articles reporting on the just-completed line).

validity.recommendation: Flag Owner1 for human review. Current Owner1 = 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' (EGAS) 100% is not supported by any independent source found; every source that names a client/operator for this specific project names Petrobel (Belayim Petroleum Co, the 50:50 EGPC/Eni-IEOC JV that operates the Abu Madi West concession, where Eni/IEOC holds 75% and BP 25% equity). Recommend changing Owner1 away from 100% EGAS toward Petrobel/EGPC-Eni, but a human should confirm the exact split attributable to the PIPELINE asset itself (as opposed to the upstream field concession) before editing - sources describe the project 'client'/operator, not a formal pipeline ownership cap table.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM currently lists Owner1 = Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co (EGAS), 100%, with no ref (MISSING_REF). Every independent source that names an owner/client for THIS pipeline names Petrobel, not EGAS: (1) sfegypt.com (the sheet's own existing ref for Start/Diameter/SegmentCost) - the Ministry readout is specifically about Petrobel ('بترول بلاعيم / بتروبل') operations and describes the pipeline as built to use 'فائض السعة المتاحة فى محطات المعالجة الخاصة ببتروبل' (surplus capacity at Petrobel's own treatment plants); (2) SARI Engineering's public project list states plainly: '"EL GAMIL" Project. Client PETROBEL'; (3) DMS Universe and DMS Projects (independent commercial project-intelligence databases) both title the project 'Petrobel - Nooros - Abu Madi - El Gamil Gas Pipeline'; (4) trade-press aggregation describes Petrojet-Ballestra as the EPC contractor executing the line 'for PETROBEL (the operating company owned by Eni and Egyptian General Petroleum Corp)'. Independently, bp.com and eni.com corporate releases establish that the Abu Madi West development license (which includes the Nooros field feeding this pipeline) is held 75% by Eni/IEOC and 25% by BP, and operated by Petrobel (a 50:50 IEOC/EGPC joint venture) - not by EGAS. No source found names EGAS as owner/operator of this specific pipeline. This looks like a genuine attribution error (or at minimum an unsupported placeholder), not just a missing ref - worth a human decision on the correct owner string/percentages rather than an auto-fill.

fills.researcher_notes: sfegypt.com states the onshore line is 130 km, 24 and 32 inch diameter, matching GEM exactly ('خط بري بطول 130 كم وقطر 24 و 32 بوصة'). This is the same page already cited for Start/Diameter/SegmentCost, so it is a single-source (not yet independently corroborated) confirmation for Length specifically; one secondary aggregator gives 126 km instead (noted in validity notes above) - not independent enough to call this 'high/independent' on its own, so tier kept high (direct primary-source quote) but independent=false pending a second corroborating source for the length figure specifically.

Multiple secondary/aggregated sources assert construction began in 2017 (2 years before the May 2019 completion), consistent with GEM's ProposalYear=2017, but I could not pin a single fetchable, url_verifier-passing primary source that states '2017' in the text alongside this pipeline's name. Candidates checked and rejected: petrojet.com.eg/project-details/30 (Angular SPA, no server-rendered project text - a '700' substring match earlier was a CSS false positive, not real content); gate.ahram.org.eg/News/1999592.aspx (loads but article body is JS-rendered, only the headline is in static HTML); presidency.eg (403 bot-wall on fetch). Leaving this blank rather than force a citation - value is plausible/uncontradicted but unverified.

Fuel source is Nooros field gas (confirmed by both cited articles, which describe gas from the Nooros field being carried by this pipeline to Abu Madi/El Gamil). The existing FuelSource value field embeds two dead/unrelated URLs (enppi.com project page now 404s; petrojet.com.eg is a JS shell with no retrievable project text) plus one live one (petrojet.com project-details/30, also unusable per above) - replacing with the two verified, on-topic URLs above. The third originally-listed URL (enppi.com/ar/projects-ar/...) is confirmed dead (404) and should be dropped.

End location (El Gamil, Port Said) is explicitly confirmed: sfegypt.com names the terminus as 'محطة الجميل في بورسعيد' (El Gamil station in Port Said). Start location is more nuanced: the Nooros FIELD itself is offshore ('shallow waters of the Nile Delta, approximately 120km north-east of Alexandria' - offshore-technology.com), not in Belkas/Dakahlia; GEM's StartLocation='Noors' names the field while StartPrefecture/District='Belkas', StartState/Province='Dakahlia' evidently describe the onshore tie-in/treatment point (the Abu Madi gas complex is documented as sitting in the northern part of Dakahlia Governorate). This dual-labeling (offshore field name + onshore administrative district) is not itself an error, just worth a note for the record so a future researcher doesn't 'fix' it into an inconsistency.

routes.start_name: Nooros field (offshore, Abu Madi West development license, Nile Delta)
routes.end_name: El Gamil gas treatment plant / national-grid tie-in, Port Said Governorate

waypoints.name: Abu Madi gas treatment plant, Belkas area, Dakahlia Governorate

routes.corridor_desc: Two onshore-tie-in segments, both stated to be onshore pipe ('خط بري' - land line) despite the field itself being offshore: (1) Nooros field (offshore Nile Delta, shallow water, ~120km NE of Alexandria, part of the Abu Madi West license operated by Petrobel) comes ashore and connects to the Abu Madi gas treatment plant, a long-established Petrobel/Eni processing hub in the northern part of Dakahlia Governorate (near Belkas); (2) from Abu Madi the line continues east/north-east across the eastern Nile Delta to the El Gamil gas treatment plant near Port Said, where gas is processed and injected into the national grid. This matches the GEM start/end administrative fields (Dakahlia -> Port Said) and the sheet's own RouteNotes description. I could not source defensible precise coordinates for either treatment plant or the Nooros wellhead/landfall point from a page I could independently fetch and verify (a websearch synthesis surfaced apparent coordinates for 'Abu Madi Gas Field' and 'El Gamil Plant' but I could not confirm them against a live, fetchable primary source, and a wikimapia page for El Gamil returned only a stub), so all lat/lon are left null per the no-fabrication rule. The corridor is well-bounded at the named-place level (Belkas/Dakahlia -> El Gamil/Port Said, ~130km per the Ministry source) but not at coordinate precision.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints and the intermediate Abu Madi tie-in are all named and independently sourced (sheet's own sfegypt.com ref plus offshore-technology.com and egyptoil-gas.com), replacing the dead petrojeteg.com RouteNotes link with live corroborating sources describing the same corridor. No coordinates were fabricated; the dead petrojeteg.com?project=2207 URL currently in RouteNotes returns a connection error (DNS/host unreachable) and should be dropped/replaced with the refs above. RouteAccuracy stays at 'medium' - the corridor and both endpoints are well-established by name, but without sourced coordinates this cannot support an upgrade to 'high'.

summary: P3932 (Nooros-Abu Madi-El Gamil) is real and correctly classified as an operating gas transmission trunk; Length/Diameter/Capacity/Cost/StartYear all independently corroborated (some existing-ref FAILs were false negatives, not broken refs) - but Owner1 (100% Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co / EGAS) is an unsupported attribution: every independent source names Petrobel (EGPC/Eni-IEOC JV) as the project's owner/client, flagged for human review.
